claims.text: On 17 May 2026 the WHO Director-General determined that the epidemic of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the DRC and Uganda constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

WHO Disease Outbreak News #613 (17 July 2026): as of 15 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported 2,124 confirmed cases including 828 deaths (case fatality ratio 39%), with Ituri province the most affected (27 of 36 health zones; 89.6% of cases, 83.6% of deaths), and further cases in North Kivu (11 of 34 health zones), South Kivu (1 of 34 health zones), Haut-Uele (4 of 13 health zones) and Tshopo (3 of 23 health zones). As of 17 July 2026, Uganda reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths in imported cases plus one probable case resulting in death. WHO assessed the risk as very high nationally in DRC due to ongoing transmission and expansion into new health zones, high in Uganda due to confirmed cross-border spread, high for countries sharing land borders with the affected countries, and low for the rest of the African region and globally.

Page last updated 21 July 2026, 17:00. On 20 July 2026 (data up until 19 July), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 2,423 confirmed cases including 967 related deaths, an increase of 79 new confirmed cases and 37 deaths since the previous update; 734 patients are hospitalised in isolation and 469 have recovered. Ituri province remains the most affected, with 2,160 cases including 811 deaths, reported from 28 of 36 health zones (up from 27/36); North Kivu has reported 239 cases including 141 deaths from 11 of 34 health zones; South Kivu 3 cases including 1 death from 1 of 34 health zones; Haut-Uele 16 cases including 10 deaths from 4 of 13 health zones; and Tshopo 5 cases including 4 deaths from 3 of 23 health zones — 47 of 140 health zones affected in total, still across the same five provinces (no new province reported). Uganda has reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths, with the last confirmed case on 21 June and no new cases since; its last patient was discharged on 16 July, and the 42-day countdown toward declaring Uganda's outbreak over is ongoing.

Page last updated 22 July 2026, 16:50. As of 21 July 2026 (data up until 20 July), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 2,473 confirmed cases including 999 related deaths, an increase of 50 new confirmed cases and 32 deaths since the previous day; 737 patients are hospitalised in isolation and 482 have recovered. Ituri province remains the most affected, with 2,202 cases including 838 deaths, reported from 28 of 36 health zones; North Kivu has reported 247 cases including 146 deaths from 11 of 34 health zones; South Kivu 3 cases including 1 death from 1 of 34 health zones; Haut-Uele 16 cases including 10 deaths from 4 of 13 health zones; and Tshopo 5 cases including 4 deaths from 3 of 23 health zones — 47 of 140 health zones affected in total, still across the same five provinces. Uganda has reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths, with the last confirmed case on 21 June and no new cases since, its 42-day countdown toward declaring Uganda's outbreak over continuing.

Page last updated 23 July 2026, 13:36. As of 22 July 2026 (data up until 21 July), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 2,536 confirmed cases, including 1,033 related deaths, an increase of 63 new confirmed cases and 34 deaths since the previous day. Ituri province remains the most affected with 2,248 cases, 864 deaths (28 of 36 health zones); North Kivu has reported 259 cases, 152 deaths (11 of 34 health zones); South Kivu 3 cases, 1 death (1 of 34 health zones); Haut-Uele 21 cases, 12 deaths (4 of 13 health zones); and Tshopo 5 cases, 4 deaths (3 of 23 health zones) — 47 of 140 health zones are currently affected across the five provinces. Uganda has reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths; the last confirmed case was reported on 17 July as 20 cases with two deaths, the final patient was discharged on 16 July, and Uganda's 42-day countdown to declaring the end of the outbreak continues.

Page last updated 24 July 2026, 15:23. As of 23 July 2026 (data up until 22 July), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 2,905 confirmed cases, including 1,269 related deaths. Ituri province remains the most affected with 2,595 cases, 1,077 deaths (28 of 36 health zones); North Kivu has reported 275 cases, 172 deaths (11 of 34 health zones); South Kivu 3 cases, 1 death (1 of 34 health zones); Haut-Uele 27 cases, 15 deaths (4 of 13 health zones); and Tshopo 5 cases, 4 deaths (3 of 23 health zones) — 47 of 140 health zones affected across the five provinces. Uganda has reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths, with the last confirmed case on 21 June and no new cases since; its last patient was discharged on 16 July, and the 42-day countdown toward declaring Uganda's outbreak over continues.

Page last updated 27 July 2026, 15:00. As of 25 July 2026 (data up until 25 July), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 3,200 confirmed cases, including 1,405 related deaths. Uganda has reported a total of 20 confirmed cases, including two deaths, as reported by the Ministry of Health as of 17 July 2026, with no new cases since 21 June and its 42-day countdown toward declaring Uganda's outbreak over continuing.

Page last updated 28 July 2026. As of 26 July 2026 (data up until 26 July), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 3,262 confirmed cases, including 1,437 related deaths. Uganda remains unchanged at 20 confirmed cases including two deaths, with no new cases since 21 June and its 42-day countdown toward declaring Uganda's outbreak over continuing.

Page last updated 29 July 2026, 16:30. On 28 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported a total of 3,360 confirmed cases, including 1,487 related deaths (from data up until 27 July). On 16 July, Uganda discharged the last Ebola patient who had been receiving treatment at the Mulago National Referral Isolation Centre; on 28 July 2026, twelve days since the last case was discharged, Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the end of the Ebola disease outbreak. Uganda's cumulative total remains 20 confirmed cases and two deaths.

Page last updated 31 July 2026, 14:30. As of 28 July 2026 (data up until 27 July), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 3,442 confirmed cases, including 1,521 related deaths, an increase of 82 new confirmed cases and 34 deaths since the previous update; 797 patients are hospitalised in isolation, and 49 of 140 health zones are affected. Uganda remains unchanged at 20 confirmed cases including two deaths, with no new cases since 21 June; the country's outbreak was declared ended on 28 July 2026.

WHO Disease Outbreak News #614 (published 1 August 2026): "As of 30 July 2026, a total of 3605 confirmed cases, including 1587 deaths, have been reported, corresponding to a crude case fatality ratio (CFR) of 44%." Cases span 49 health zones across five provinces: Ituri (28/36), North Kivu (11/34), South Kivu (1/34), Haut-Uele (5/13) and Tshopo (4/23). The outbreak is now the largest recorded Ebola virus disease outbreak in the country, surpassing the 2018-2020 outbreak (3,317 confirmed cases). On 28 July, Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the end of the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the country, following 42 days without a new confirmed locally transmitted case after the last confirmed case was discharged from care on 16 June 2026.

In total, 1481 confirmed cases; 1460 from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 20 from Uganda and one from France (linked to DRC); and 454 deaths including two from Uganda, have been reported. As of 1 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo had reported 1,460 confirmed cases including 452 deaths (case fatality ratio 30.9%) and 213 recovered; as of 2 July 2026 Uganda had reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths and one probable case (deceased), with 16 recovered.

Page last updated 4 August 2026, 14:30. As of 3 August 2026 (data up until 2 August), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 3,802 confirmed cases, including 1,707 related deaths, with 707 patients hospitalised in isolation. Provincial breakdown: Ituri 3,317 cases/1,382 deaths (28 of 36 health zones); North Kivu 414 cases/285 deaths (12 of 34 health zones); South Kivu 3 cases/1 death (1 of 34 health zones); Haut-Uele 61 cases/34 deaths (5 of 13 health zones); Tshopo 7 cases/5 deaths (5 of 23 health zones) — 51 of 140 health zones affected across the five provinces. Uganda's outbreak remains ended (declared 28 July 2026) with its cumulative total unchanged at 20 confirmed cases and two deaths.

Page last updated 5 August 2026, 17:00. As of 4 August 2026 (data up until 3 August), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 3,874 confirmed cases, including 1,751 related deaths, with 717 patients hospitalised in isolation — an increase of 72 confirmed cases and 44 deaths since the 4 August update. Provincial breakdown: Ituri 3,375 cases/1,417 deaths (28 of 36 health zones); North Kivu 426 cases/290 deaths (12 of 34 health zones); South Kivu 3 cases/1 death (1 of 34 health zones); Haut-Uele 63 cases/38 deaths (5 of 13 health zones); Tshopo 7 cases/5 deaths (5 of 23 health zones) — 51 of 140 health zones affected across the five provinces. Uganda's outbreak remains ended (declared 28 July 2026) with its cumulative total unchanged at 20 confirmed cases and two deaths.

ECDC's country overview (page last updated 6 August 2026 13:45) reports the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now recorded 3,973 confirmed cases including 1,801 related deaths, from data up until 4 August 2026 -- up from 3,874 cases/1,751 deaths as of the prior 3 August data cut. Uganda's outbreak remains unchanged at 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, declared ended 28 July 2026.

ECDC's country overview (page last updated 7 August 2026 15:40) now reports the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 4,053 confirmed cases including 1,850 related deaths, from data up until 5 August 2026 -- up from 3,973 cases/1,801 deaths as of the prior 4 August data cut, and noting: "Data reported by DRC on confirmed cases and deaths are under continuous review and harmonisation." 53 of 140 health zones are now affected across the same five provinces. Uganda's outbreak remains unchanged at 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, declared ended 28 July 2026. WHO's Disease Outbreak News series remains at DON614 (1 August 2026, data to 30 July), with no DON615 yet published.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: ECDC's country overview (updated 7 August 2026, data as of 5 August 2026) is unchanged since the prior check — the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 4,053 confirmed cases including 1,850 related deaths; Uganda's outbreak remains ended at 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths. WHO's Disease Outbreak News series remains at DON614 (1 August 2026, data to 30 July), with no DON615 yet published.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: per data reported by the DRC on 6 August 2026 (data through 5 August 2026), ECDC records 4,053 confirmed cases including 1,850 related deaths -- the death toll is unchanged from the prior check, with 80 new confirmed cases and 49 additional deaths recorded in the 5 August update relative to the previous day. ECDC notes this is now the largest recorded Ebola outbreak in DRC's history, surpassing the 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak. Separately, Uganda's linked outbreak was declared over by Uganda's Ministry of Health on 28 July 2026, following discharge of the last patient on 16 July and 12 days without new cases; the DRC outbreak itself remains ongoing.

Re-checked 11 August 2026: ECDC's country overview (page last updated 10 August 2026, 14:50, data as of 7 August 2026) now reports the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 4,209 confirmed cases including 1,916 related deaths, an increase of 89 new confirmed cases and 21 deaths since the prior 5 August data cut (4,053 cases/1,850 deaths). Uganda's outbreak remains ended (declared 28 July 2026) with its cumulative total unchanged at 20 confirmed cases and two deaths. WHO's Disease Outbreak News series remains at DON614 (1 August 2026, data to 30 July), with no DON615 yet published.

Re-checked 12 August 2026: ECDC's country overview (page last updated 11 August 2026, 16:50, data as of 9 August 2026) now reports the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 4,381 confirmed cases including 2,011 related deaths -- up from 4,209 cases/1,916 deaths as of the prior 7 August data cut -- with 704 patients hospitalised in isolation and 86.7% of identified case contacts under follow-up. 53 of 140 health zones remain affected across the same five provinces. Uganda's outbreak remains ended (declared 28 July 2026) with its cumulative total unchanged at 20 confirmed cases and two deaths. WHO's Disease Outbreak News series remains at DON614 (1 August 2026, data to 30 July), with no DON615 yet published; WHO's Ebola-DRC-2026 situation page's most recent news item (11 August 2026) announces a US$3 million Wellcome grant for community-evidence gathering, not a new case-count release.

ECDC's country overview (page updated 12 August 2026, data as of 10 August 2026): the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported a total of 4,449 confirmed cases including 2,061 related deaths, with 716 patients hospitalised in isolation -- an increase of 68 confirmed cases and 50 deaths since the previous update; 82.7% of identified case contacts are under follow-up across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo provinces; 53 of 140 health zones are currently affected.

ECDC country overview (page last updated 13 August 2026 13:34, data as of 11 August 2026): "On 12 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) published a situation update reporting a total of 4 566 confirmed cases, including 2 128 related deaths (from data up until 11 August). A total of 570 patients are hospitalised in isolation. This represents an increase of 117 new confirmed cases and 67 deaths since the previous report on 11 August (reporting data up until 10 August). In total, 82.4% of identified case contacts are under follow-up in the Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo provinces. Overall, 53 of 140 health zones are currently affected across the five provinces."
As of 4 July, the country's [DRC] Government has recorded 1,561 confirmed cases, including 506 deaths and 254 people recovered. More than 10,000 contacts are being monitored.

ECDC's Weekly Communicable Disease Threats Report (Week 33, 8-14 Aug 2026) and WHO Disease Outbreak News 2026-DON615 (published 14 Aug 2026) confirm, as of 12-13 August 2026: DRC has recorded 4,665 confirmed cases and 2,184 deaths (crude case fatality ratio 46.8%), the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the country, now spanning a sixth province (Bas-Uele) and 54 of 151 health zones. Uganda's linked outbreak (20 cases, 2 deaths) was declared ended by its Ministry of Health on 28 July 2026 after 12 days with no new case.

As of 9 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported a total of 1,792 confirmed cases, including 625 related deaths (from data up until 8 July), an increase of 33 new confirmed cases and 25 related deaths since the prior update, with cases concentrated in Ituri province (1,631 cases, 535 deaths) and North Kivu (158 cases, 89 deaths). Uganda has reported a total of 20 confirmed cases, including two deaths, with the last confirmed case reported on 21 June and no new cases since.

On 12 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported a total of 1,926 confirmed cases, including 702 related deaths (from data up until 11 July). A total of 753 patients are hospitalised in isolation. Ituri province remains the most affected, with 1,745 cases, including 601 deaths, reported from 26 of 36 health zones. In North Kivu, 73 cases, including 97 deaths, have been reported from 11 of 34 health zones. In South Kivu, three cases, including one death, have been reported from one of 34 health zones. In Haut-Uele, one case has been reported and in Tshopo four cases. As of 12 July 2026, in Uganda a total of 20 confirmed cases, including two deaths, have been reported by the Ministry of Health; the last confirmed case was reported on 21 June with no new cases since. On 10 July 2026, the US CDC reported that a US citizen working for a humanitarian organisation in DRC had tested positive for Bundibugyo virus; the patient was medically evacuated to Germany on 13 July 2026, in addition to an imported case reported in France on 24 June 2026.

On 13 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported a total of 1,963 confirmed cases, including 719 related deaths (data up until 12 July), an increase of 31 new confirmed cases and 10 deaths since the previous update; 736 patients are hospitalised in isolation and 333 have recovered. Ituri province remains the most affected, with 1,772 cases including 608 deaths, reported from 26 of 36 health zones; North Kivu has reported 177 cases including 100 deaths; South Kivu 3 cases including 1 death; Haut-Uele 7 cases including 7 deaths; and Tshopo 4 cases including 3 deaths. Uganda has reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths, with the last confirmed case on 21 June and no new cases since.

On 14 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported a total of 2,011 confirmed cases, including 754 related deaths (data up until 13 July), an increase of 54 new confirmed cases and 28 deaths since the previous update; 753 patients are hospitalised in isolation and 366 have recovered. Ituri province remains the most affected, with 1,808 cases including 631 deaths, reported from 26 of 36 health zones; North Kivu has reported 182 cases including 106 deaths; South Kivu 3 cases including 1 death; Haut-Uele 14 cases including 13 deaths; and Tshopo 4 cases including 3 deaths — 45 of 140 health zones affected in total. Uganda has reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths, with the last confirmed case on 21 June and no new cases since; 67.4% of identified case contacts in affected provinces are under follow-up.

WHO Director-General's opening remarks at the media briefing of 16 July 2026: "So far, 2073 cases have been reported, with 796 deaths" in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. "In Uganda, the last confirmed case is being discharged from care today, starting the 42-day countdown" toward declaring the country's outbreak over, with 20 cases and two deaths.

As of 14 July 2026 (data up until 14 July), the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported 2,073 confirmed cases including 796 related deaths. Ituri province remains the most affected with 1,863 cases including 668 deaths, reported from 26 of 36 health zones; North Kivu has reported 189 cases including 111 deaths; South Kivu 3 cases including 1 death; Haut-Uele 14 cases including 13 deaths; and Tshopo 4 cases including 3 deaths. Uganda has reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths; its last confirmed case, reported on 21 June, was discharged from care on 16 July 2026 after two negative tests, starting the 42-day countdown toward declaring Uganda's outbreak over.

description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo declared its 17th Ebola outbreak — caused by Bundibugyo virus — on 15 May 2026, centred in Ituri Province. On 17 May 2026 the WHO Director-General declared the DRC and Uganda epidemic a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Confirmed cases and deaths have continued to climb through early August (3,874 cases/1,751 deaths in DRC per ECDC, page updated 5 August 2026, data to 3 August), with the outbreak now the largest recorded Ebola virus disease outbreak in DRC history, still confined to the same five DRC provinces, and imported cases previously confirmed in France and Germany. Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the end of its outbreak on 28 July 2026, twelve days after discharging its last confirmed patient, with a final Ugandan toll of 20 confirmed cases and two deaths and no new cases since 21 June. ECDC's country overview (page last updated 7 August 2026 15:40) now reports the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 4,053 confirmed cases including 1,850 related deaths, from data up until 5 August 2026 -- up from 3,973 cases/1,801 deaths as of the prior 4 August data cut, and noting: "Data reported by DRC on confirmed cases and deaths are under continuous review and harmonisation." 53 of 140 health zones are now affected across the same five provinces. Uganda's outbreak remains unchanged at 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, declared ended 28 July 2026. WHO's Disease Outbreak News series remains at DON614 (1 August 2026, data to 30 July), with no DON615 yet published. Re-checked 9 August 2026: ECDC's country overview (updated 7 August 2026, data as of 5 August) is unchanged — DRC 4,053 confirmed cases and 1,850 deaths; Uganda's outbreak remains ended (20 cases, 2 deaths). WHO's Disease Outbreak News series remains at DON614 (1 August 2026); no DON615 has been published. Re-checked 10 August 2026: ECDC confirms 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths (data as of 5 August 2026), unchanged from the prior check, and notes this is now the largest recorded Ebola outbreak in DRC's history. Uganda's linked outbreak was declared over on 28 July 2026; the DRC outbreak remains ongoing. Re-checked 11 August 2026: ECDC's country overview (page last updated 10 August 2026, 14:50, data as of 7 August 2026) now reports the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 4,209 confirmed cases including 1,916 related deaths, an increase of 89 confirmed cases and 21 deaths from the prior 5 August data cut (4,053 cases/1,850 deaths); Uganda's outbreak remains ended (20 confirmed cases, 2 deaths, declared over 28 July 2026); no WHO DON615 has been published, with DON614 (1 August 2026) still the latest in that series. Re-checked 12 August 2026: ECDC's country overview (page last updated 11 August 2026, data as of 9 August 2026) now reports the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 4,381 confirmed cases including 2,011 related deaths, up from 4,209 cases/1,916 deaths as of the prior 7 August data cut; 704 patients are hospitalised in isolation. Uganda's outbreak remains ended (20 cases, 2 deaths, declared over 28 July 2026); no WHO DON615 has been published, with DON614 (1 August 2026) still the latest in that series. ECDC's 12 August 2026 update (data as of 10 August) puts the DRC total at 4,449 confirmed cases and 2,061 deaths, an increase of 68 cases and 50 deaths since the prior update; the outbreak continues to expand, and Uganda's linked outbreak remains declared over since 28 July 2026. Re-checked 14 August 2026: ECDC's country overview (data as of 11 August 2026) reports 4,566 confirmed cases including 2,128 related deaths, up from 4,449 cases/2,061 deaths as of the prior data cut. Uganda's outbreak remains ended; no WHO DON615 has been published, with DON614 (1 August 2026) still the latest in that series. Re-checked 15 August 2026: ECDC's country overview (published 13 August 2026, data as of 12 August 2026) reports 4,665 confirmed cases including 2,184 related deaths in DRC, up from 4,566 cases/2,128 deaths as of the prior 11 August data cut (an increase of 99 cases and 56 deaths). WHO's Regional Office for Africa Weekly External Situation Report 13 separately gives a slightly lower, earlier cut (4,381 cases, 2,011 deaths as of 9 August, CFR 45.9%), consistent with different reporting cutoffs rather than a contradiction. Uganda's outbreak remains ended (20 cases, 2 deaths, declared over 28 July 2026); no WHO DON615 has been published, with DON614 (1 August 2026) still the latest in that series. Re-checked 16 August 2026: DRC's confirmed toll is unchanged at 4,665 cases and 2,184 deaths (data as of 12-13 August, per WHO DON 2026-DON615 and ECDC's Week 33 report); the outbreak has expanded to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, and now affects 54 of 151 health zones. Uganda's linked outbreak remains formally declared over (28 July 2026).
